fixed: Deferred terminal refocus now rechecks workspace interaction guards
Runtime QML warning publication is bounded and reentrancy-safe
Unchanged supervisor ticks preserve queue delegates instead of rebuilding controls
Typed IDs remain explicit in opaque request tokens; isolated same-token neighbor drafts are asserted
Private fixture ownership survives startup/cleanup errors and cancellation; complete response identities are verified independently of array order
Live probe uses verified session IDs, checks visible partial-draft restoration and rejects duplicate role/endpoint configuration
Probe callbacks have scoped lifetimes and report assertions outside event callbacks; clipboard backup is shared and restores all MIME data
Timing starts before all command bytes, uses monotonic nanoseconds and states its frame callback endpoint/current versus peak RSS
Synthetic shortcut presses have matching releases; real-window eligibility is checked before clock-driven cases
Complex methods split around actual responsibilities; unchecked optional, container allocation and narrowing warnings repaired
consolidation: Removed unused Python configuration validator and unused prompt plus tests that only exercised those dead paths
Shared explicit Codex probe configuration arguments replace positional app-server argument slicing; complete server argv compared equal to previous implementation
Shared clipboard backup replaces copied native/workspace implementations
README owns current status, architecture owns acceptance, CONTRIBUTING owns procedures; removed duplicate historical narrative and stale planned-status text
review_dispositions: Opening a stale/submitted request remains intentional inspection; source validation disables every response. Viewing is not approval.
Repeated explicit Snooze extends its deadline by design; it does not retire attention or affect other sources.
Qt 6.11.2 declares failChildProcessModifier Q_NORETURN; the reported continuation path is unreachable.
No lower universal analysis concurrency cap was added without measured resource evidence; this run used six jobs on the 16-thread host.
Broad process/protocol fixture consolidation was not forced across distinct lifecycle and safety contracts. Owned service process-group guards and bounded disappearance checks remain authoritative.
Native synchronous paste guarding, Qt release behavior, scheduled timer execution and live routing are separate complementary checks.

notes: Early live startup/identity and manifest setup defects were fixed before the passing qualification.
A pre-rebuild live attempt in live-final used the older GUI binary and reported an interrupted turn; it is excluded. The rebuilt live-draft and live-qualified runs passed with cleanup.
A missing worker helper was caught by compilation and repaired by the coordinator; worker completion was not treated as verification.
Initial timing clicked an offscreen Stack card; measurement now starts at Workspace::setFocusedIndex and ends at the explicit frame callback.

Some intermediate GUI/input runs failed transiently; exact causes were not established for all cases. Retained logs include these failures. Final complete desktop run, native input, controls, live dialogs and both sanitizer reruns passed.

limits: Two-session qualification only; eight-entry storage/1024-request bounds do not qualify larger workloads.
Thirty controlled warm-switch and shell-output samples; no continuous background load or 32-session claim.
frameSwapped callbacks are not physical input-to-photon measurements. GPU utilization, service memory and unified GPU allocation are not measured by this GUI RSS/idle baseline.
One-second idle CPU/RSS observations are dated samples, not performance gates or proof of bounded long-run memory growth.
Vendor Qt/MoltenVK/Ghostty are uninstrumented; selected sanitizer suites are not complete vendor coverage.
macOS only. Linux desktop, second CLI adapter, automatic service-death/reboot recovery, selection/accessibility/shaping expansion and binary redistribution remain outside Milestone 3.
Physical typing is not an acceptance gate; native OS input is automated.
